compliance.seismic: Designed to comply with Zone 4 earthquake requirements per NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 3 (Table 30 wording)

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 2000 m (6562 ft)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing (up to 93 percent short term)
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.optics: 100 GbE QSFP28, 40 GbE QSFP+, AOC, DAC and breakout cables; a QSFP+ to SFP+ adapter (QSA) from Junos OS 19.3R1
features.timing: RJ45 grand master clock jack (GM), 1 PPS output, 10 MHz output
features.virtual-chassis: up to three QFX5200-32C members (not the 32C-L)

management.oob: SFP management cages C0 and C1 and an RJ45 C0 (10/100/1000 BASE-T); the 32C-L has no second management interface

performance.port-speeds: QSFP28 ports 0 to 31, 100 GbE by default; 50, 40, 25 or 10 GbE by configuration or with a breakout cable (up to 128 logical ports)

physical.weight-note: 23.5 lb (10.66 kg) fully loaded, QFX5200-32C and QFX5200-32C-L (Table 31)

power.power-input-ac: 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 4.5 A at 100 to 120 VAC or 2.0 A at 200 to 240 VAC
power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating range -40 to -72 VDC, 10 A maximum
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, load-sharing; one may be removed at a time while the switch runs

thermal.fans: five fan modules; the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced

configs.description: QFX5200-32C-AFI: two 850 W AC supplies (JPSU-850W-AC-AFI) and five back-to-front fan modules (QFX5200-32C-FANAFI). All carry the label AIR IN and a Juniper Azure Blue handle (guide Tables 17 and 19).
configs.name: ac-afi

configs.description: QFX5200-32C-AFO: two 850 W AC supplies (JPSU-850W-AC-AFO) and five front-to-back fan modules (QFX5200-32C-FANAFO). All carry the label AIR OUT and a Juniper Gold handle (guide Tables 17 and 19).
configs.name: ac-afo

configs.description: Two DC supplies (JPSU-850W-DC-AFI) and five back-to-front fan modules (QFX5200-32C-FANAFI). The guide names these units but no chassis part number for the build.
configs.name: dc-afi

configs.description: QFX5200-32C-DC: two DC supplies (JPSU-850W-DC-AFO) and five front-to-back fan modules (QFX5200-32C-FANAFO). The guide names the DC build QFX5200-32C-DC and does not say its airflow; the front-to-back supply is the one seated, like the AC default. AC and DC supplies are never mixed in one 32C.
configs.name: dc-afo

configs.description: QFX5200-32C-LAFI: the QFX5200-32C-L with two 850 W AC supplies (JPSU-850W-AC-AFI) and five back-to-front fan modules (QFX5200-32C-FANAFI, shared with the -AFI build). The -32C-L takes AC supplies only and has no second management interface (C1).
configs.name: l-ac-afi

configs.description: QFX5200-32C-LAFO: the QFX5200-32C-L, the same port panel running Junos OS Evolved, with two 850 W AC supplies (JPSU-850W-AC-AFO) and five front-to-back fan modules (QFX5200-32C-FANAFO, shared with the -AFO build). The -32C-L takes AC supplies only and has no second management interface (C1).
configs.name: l-ac-afo

gaps.wanted: The two green lamps in the corners of the GM jack that the studio photograph shows. The guide's port panel text describes none.
The connector family of PPS OUT and 10M OUT (drawn as SMA from the photograph). The guide names the outputs and no connector.
Whether a C1 legend is printed at the lower SFP cage, and which of C0 and C1 each cage is. No photograph of the FRU side exists and figure 41's legends are small.
A straight-on photograph of the FRU side. The suggested studio address answered 404. The FRU side is drawn from the guide's raster figures alone, estimated.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port and gives no generation, so the port is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin and no colour is claimed.
The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port group qsfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: guide Table 31: 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.1 cm) wide, 20.48 in (52 cm) deep, 23.5 lb (10.66 kg), for the QFX5200-32C and the QFX5200-32C-L. The inch figures are converted (43.69, 440.94 and 520.19 mm) because the centimetre figures are rounded to one digit; the centimetre figures agree to the rounding. The width is the body between the ear folds: the guide says the front mounting brackets extend it to 19 in, so the brackets are not modelled.

clock-block.note: The RJ45 grand master clock jack GM, the PPS OUT jack and the 10M OUT jack, at the left. Figure 14 and the photograph agree on the housing (16.8 x 14.0 mm over the jack's 15.8 x 13.2), 8.9 mm down and 18.8 mm in. The two outputs are 15.0 mm apart, 8.1 mm across their nuts, with the legends above. The guide names them only as 1PPS output and 10 MHz output; THE CONNECTOR FAMILY IS ESTIMATED AS SMA from the photograph (knurled barrel and hex nut of about 8 mm), not stated by any document. The photograph also shows two green lamps in the corners of the GM jack; the guide describes no lamp there, so none is drawn.

colour.note: The front plate samples #9399a1 and #959ca4 on two bare patches of the right-hand plate; the chassis colour is #949aa2. The photograph is lit warmly and these are its values, not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: The guide describes mounting flush with the front of a four-post 19 in rack with the standard brackets, or recessed 2 in (5 cm) with the extension bracket, for the 32C and 32C-L only. Both are written as ear positions with no kit. The rack mount kits the guide names are NOT MODELLED and are not in `chassis.kits`: JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E, shipped with the switch (a pair of front and rear rails, a pair of brackets, sixteen M4 x 6 mm screws), whose spare is also sold as EX-4PST-RMK. The guide's rail spacing is 23.5 to 30.6 in (59.7 to 77.7 cm) front to back. The recessed position's -50.8 mm is the guide's 2 in; no figure measures it.

esd-and-labels.note: At the right: the ESD terminal (callout 5), a 4.4 mm hole centred 417.5 mm across and 16.7 down, with the ESD symbol beneath at 25.1 mm; a laser hazard triangle at about 412.6 and 27.4, which is 8.5 mm across on the photograph and is drawn with the library's 5.4 mm part; and a yellow LASER RADIATION label 24.1 x 5.1 mm at the foot. The guide draws two blank label areas and no triangle, so THE PHOTOGRAPH WINS and the triangle and the label are drawn from it. The label's small print is not transcribed.

gate-1.note: Figure 14 (a 3559 x 650 px raster of the port side) is orthographic enough to measure: its outline measures 3420 px between stroke centres (x 50.5 to 3470.5) and 338.5 px (y 279.5 to 618), an aspect of 10.10 against the table's 440.94 / 43.69 = 10.09, at 7.755 px/mm both ways. The studio photograph agrees (body 51 to 2063 px, 4.56 px/mm, 199 px high, 43.6 mm) and was used to confirm the figure. Figure 19 (the FRU side, a 756 px raster) reads 716.5 px between its side edges, 1.625 px/mm, but only 67.5 px high, 5 percent short of the table, so its horizontal scale is used and its vertical scale is fitted to the table's height.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. No Juniper notice was found and the guide states none. A third-party tracker (router-switch.com) lists an announcement of 2021-01-20 and end of sale of 2021-10-04 for the QFX5200-32C-AFO, -AFI and -T builds and 2024-11-15 for the -SAFO, -SAFI, -DCSAFO and -DCSAFI builds, so the device states none announced. Estimated, because the tracker is not the maker.

mgmt-panel.note: Figures 20 and 41: four chassis lamps (ALM, SYS, MST, ID) at the left; two stacked SFP cages at the centre left, the upper marked C0 (callout 2, with the RJ45 C0 sharing the name: for C0 the copper jack has priority over the fibre cage) and the lower the C1 cage (callout 5); an RJ45 console port at the upper right (CON, callout 3) and an RJ45 management port C0 beneath it (callout 2); a USB port; and a recessed RESET at the foot. The printed legends read from the figure are C0 above the upper cage, CON beside the console and C0 under the lower jack; no C1 legend is legible. The model plate reads QFX5200-32C and RUNNING JUNOS. The 32C-L does not support the second management interface (C1).

modules.note: The fan modules and the power supplies are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay: the supplies' own fans are inside the supplies. The supplies JPSU-850W-AC-AFO and JPSU-850W-AC-AFI are the library's existing components, reused as they are (same part number, same arrangement of lamps AC, DC and !, handle, inlet and cord retainer as figure 40 shows); their size is the bay's, an estimate recorded on those components. The fan modules are this family's own, qfx5200-32c-fan-afo and -afi, drawn from figures 19 and 27.

port-lamps.note: Four lamps a port, as figure 15 shows and Table 7 says (four bi-colour lamps for each QSFP+ port; the first is used and the rest are not used when the port is 100 GbE with a QSFP28 module, all four when the port is channelized). They are 4.17 mm apart (32.3 px) and centred on the cage, the upper row at 9.5 mm and the lower at 39.8 mm down the face (figure 14 reads 9.7 and 40.0, the photograph 9.3 and 39.7). Their size is the library's 2.0 mm lamp, as the photograph resolves them at about 1.8 mm. The guide's colours are green (link, steady; blinking for activity) and amber (blinking for beacon); Table 6 and Table 7 give them.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph and figure 14: ports 0 to 31, even above the cage on the upper row and odd below it on the lower, one numeral centred on each cage, between the cage and its lamps. Interface names are not printed and are not written; the guide's channelization text names no interface names for this switch.

ports.note: Figure 14, 32 QSFP28 cages in two rows of 16, in four gangs of four columns. The lamp rings sit on a 19.0 mm pitch (147.3 px), which is the registry's qsfp-ganged pitch, and the gangs are 82.0 mm apart (the studio photograph reads 82.0 as well), so the gutter is 6.0 mm. The first cage's centre is at 78.40 mm and its cell therefore starts at 69.15; the last cage's right edge falls at 391.4 mm in the figure and in the model. The rows are 13.05 mm apart on their centres (17.96 and 31.0 mm); the figure's drawn junction lines between cages read 19.5 mm, which is the drawn cage bezel and not the pitch, and the lamps and numerals are used instead because they are flat. The upper row is 13.17 mm down the face. The photograph reads 13.05 for the same edge.

power.note: Table 20 (AC): 200 W typical and 312 W maximum for the QFX5200-32C, 195 W typical for the 32C-L (312 maximum), input 100 to 240 VAC at 4.5 A (100 to 120 V) or 2.0 A (200 to 240 V), 50 to 60 Hz. Table 25 (DC): 200 W typical and 312 W maximum, -48 to -60 VDC rated, 10 A maximum. The 32C figures are filed as the device's; the 32C-L's 195 W is recorded in `attrs`.

rear-layout.note: From figure 19 alone (no photograph): a 63.4 mm management panel at the left, five fan slots on a 49.2 mm pitch from 71.4 mm with a strip before each (fan symbol, number, lamp), then two supply slots at 316.3 and 377.8 mm. These agree to 1.3 mm or better with the slot geometry the QFX5120-48Y rear photograph gives for the same chassis family (fans from 71.8 on a 49.0 pitch, supplies at 315.0 and 376.6), so the finer figures of that photograph are used for the bays, and the panel's contents are read from figure 19 and the closer figures 20 and 41. The panel contents are ESTIMATED: figure 41 is a close-up with its own scale (it is not square to the panel), so only figure 19's x scale is used and its y scale is fitted to the face height.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5200 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-03-09, 236 pages (copyright 2026 Juniper Networks): the port panel figures 12 and 14 and the LED figure 15, the management panel figures 19 and 20, the FRU panel figure 25, the fan and power supply figures 27, 34, 36, 37 and 39 to 44, the specification tables 20, 25, 30 and 31, the fan and airflow tables 3, 17 and 19 and the mounting chapter. Juniper's studio photograph of the 32C port side, 2100 x 450 px (image library, qfx5200-32c-front-high). THE HPE DATASHEET (a00150814enw) DID NOT ANSWER, a transport error on the one attempt, so no datasheet figure is used. NO PHOTOGRAPH OF THE 32C FRU SIDE WAS FOUND: the suggested qfx5200-32c-rear-high address answered 404, so the FRU side is drawn from the guide's figures 19, 20 and 41 alone. No mechanical drawing and no 3D model were found. The held intake folders (SOURCES.md, COVERAGE.md) are on another machine and could not be read from this one, so no held photograph, stencil or model was available to use.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the bright lip along the foot of every upper cage and along the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention.

vents.note: Hexagonal perforations: two staggered rows along the top edge (3.3 and 6.5 mm down), a block of five rows at the lower left (27.3 to 38.4 mm down, 7.8 to 65.3 mm across), a half row along the foot, and three columns at the right of the ports (393 to 402 mm). Drawn as vent strips on a 3.3 mm pitch; the guide's figure 14 draws the same fields. Positions are read at 4.56 px/mm and are estimated.
